question: According to Virginia Henderson, what is the main job of a nurse when caring for a patient?

options.A: To diagnose underlying pathological disease processes
options.B: To manage the entire hospital ward budget and staff
options.C: To independently prescribe medications for common illnesses
options.D: To assist the patient with activities they cannot do alone

explanation: You've got this! Henderson taught that nurses help patients regain independence by stepping in only when the patient lacks the strength, will, or knowledge to do it themselves. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is a core belief of Henderson's theory regarding a healthy human being?

options.A: They are entirely incapable of self-care during illness
options.B: They require constant supervision from healthcare providers
options.C: They focus solely on physical needs over emotional ones
options.D: They naturally strive for independence and wholeness

explanation: Henderson believed that deep down, people naturally want to be healthy, strong, and able to care for themselves whenever they can. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why does Henderson view the mind and body as connected when caring for patients?

options.A: Physical symptoms always originate from mental illness
options.B: Mental health cannot be assessed in a hospital ward
options.C: Emotional distress directly affects physical recovery
options.D: Patients only require psychological support during surgery

explanation: It's all connected! When a patient is worried or stressed emotionally, it truly affects how fast and well their physical body heals. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h2)

question: How many basic human needs form the core of Virginia Henderson's nursing theory?
explanation: There are 14 fundamental needs! Knowing these makes patient assessments much easier to break down step by step. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h3)

question: A new mother is too weak after birth to walk to the bathroom by herself. Which of Henderson's basic needs is affected here?
explanation: Spot on! Struggling to walk or change positions on her own falls directly under the need for moving and keeping good body posture. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h3)

question: What role does a nurse play when a patient is completely unconscious and unable to do anything for themselves?
explanation: When a patient cannot act for themselves at all, the nurse takes on a substitutive role—stepping in to provide total care. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h4)

question: How is a complementary nurse-patient relationship different from a substitutive one?

options.A: The nurse acts as a partner while the patient guides their own recovery
options.B: The nurse takes absolute control over every medical decision made
options.C: The doctor replaces the nurse during the primary stages of illness
options.D: The patient performs all tasks without any assistance from the nurse

explanation: Teamwork! In a complementary role, you and the patient work together like partners, helping them lead the way in their own healing journey. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the first thing a midwife does when using Henderson's theory during a patient's intake?

options.A: Assessing the patient across the 14 fundamental needs
options.B: Scheduling laboratory investigations for infectious diseases
options.C: Consulting the senior doctor for a prescribed treatment plan
options.D: Discharging the patient with written home care instructions

explanation: Care always starts with checking in! You evaluate which of the 14 needs the mother can handle alone and where she needs your helping hand. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h5)

question: A pregnant woman is so exhausted she can barely prepare her meals. According to Henderson, what should your care focus on?

options.A: Insisting that the patient manage household chores on her own
options.B: Helping the patient meet her nutritional and resting needs
options.C: Referring the patient immediately to a specialized psychiatric unit
options.D: Administering intravenous antibiotics to cure the fatigue

explanation: You've got this! By focusing on her rest and nutrition, you are directly supporting her unmet daily needs with warmth and practical care. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h5)

question: What makes Virginia Henderson's Need Theory so helpful for student midwives?

options.A: It provides a clear and straightforward framework for patient assessment
options.B: It eliminates the need for any collaboration with medical doctors
options.C: It guarantees that patients will never experience chronic illnesses
options.D: It focuses exclusively on high-tech emergency room equipment

explanation: The 14 needs give you a neat, easy-to-remember checklist to understand how your patient is doing and plan your care with confidence. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is one limitation of Henderson's model when used in modern, fast-paced hospitals?

options.A: It does not place heavy emphasis on complex, high-tech emergency crises
options.B: It completely ignores the biological and physical aspects of disease
options.C: It applies exclusively to pediatric patients in rural clinics
options.D: It makes it impossible to formulate any nursing care plans

explanation: Henderson's model is wonderful for holistic, everyday care, but it can feel a bit simple when dealing with high-tech, fast emergency room machines and crises. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h6)
